Chapter 4. Preparing Your Data

Source: vignettes/articles/04-Preparing-Your-Data.Rmd
04-Preparing-Your-Data.Rmd

Decant needs two matrices from each sample: the cells and the empty droplets. Both come from the raw (unfiltered) count matrix.

4.1 Read a 10x Genomics matrix 

# Requires your own data
raw <- read_10x_counts("sample/outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix")
dim(raw)
  • read_10x_counts() reads the three files Cell Ranger writes (matrix.mtx.gz, features.tsv.gz, barcodes.tsv.gz) and returns a sparse matrix with genes in rows and barcodes in columns.
  • By default rows are named by Ensembl gene ID (gene_column = 1), which is unique. Use gene_column = 2 for gene symbols, which some genes share.
  • Only “Gene Expression” features are kept. Antibody or CRISPR features in the same run are dropped (feature_type = NULL keeps everything).
  • A raw matrix usually has several hundred thousand columns; this is expected.

4.2 Separate cells from empty droplets 

library(Decant)
library(Matrix)
sim <- simulate_experiment(seed = 1)
colnames(sim$empty) <- paste0("empty", seq_len(ncol(sim$empty)))
raw <- Matrix(cbind(sim$observed, sim$empty), sparse = TRUE)
dim(raw)
#> [1]  600 5200

d <- split_droplets(raw, cells = colnames(sim$observed))
d$summary
#>   n_cells n_empties n_dropped soup_umis
#>      1200      4000         0    100021
  • The first four lines build a raw matrix from simulated data, so this example runs anywhere. With real data you would use the raw from 4.1.
  • split_droplets(raw, cells = ...) returns a list with cells (genes × cells), empties (genes × empty droplets) and summary.
  • cells is the vector of cell barcodes. Use the barcodes of Cell Ranger’s filtered matrix, or the cells you kept after your own quality control.
  • summary reports how many droplets went into each group and how many UMIs the soup estimate rests on (soup_umis). More than about 50,000 soup UMIs gives a stable profile.

How droplets are assigned

Droplet Rule Used as
Listed in cells always cell
Total UMIs within empty_umi_range (default 1 to 100) not a cell empty droplet
Anything else neither dropped

Droplets between the two groups are dropped on purpose: they may contain a damaged cell, and treating them as soup would bias the profile.

When you do not have a list of cells 

d2 <- split_droplets(raw)
d2$summary
#>   n_cells n_empties n_dropped soup_umis
#>      1200      4000         0    100021
  • Without cells, droplets with at least cell_min_umi (default 500) UMIs are treated as cells. This is a crude rule; a proper cell caller such as Cell Ranger, EmptyDrops or CellBender is recommended for real data.

4.3 Clusters

Decant estimates contamination cluster by cluster (Chapter 2.5), so it needs one label per cell.

# Requires your own data
clusters <- as.character(Idents(seurat_object))
  • Any clustering works: Seurat, Scanpy (imported into R), or cell-type annotations.
  • Prefer a moderate number of reasonably large clusters (for example Seurat at resolution 0.3 to 0.8). Very small clusters have too few counts to tell a weakly expressed gene from an absent one, which pushes the estimate up.
  • If you supply no clusters, Decant runs a quick k-means clustering (k = 8) itself. This is fine for exploration but less accurate.
